shots.why: first approach: the arm is going back. Cut away before the hand lets go (first refusal).
elsewhere and in colour: a board bending under a foot. Not the same person, not the same year.
same bowler, an earlier take of the approach. Cut away again, one beat later in the swing (second refusal).
1933, a man on a tower. Nothing has left yet.
third return. The hand lets go; the rattle of the ball down the lane is the first consequence the film allows.
the actual consequence: pins go down, same 1955 film. Crash sound from another bowling film (Our Community, 1952), moved here and recorded in the ledger.
phase-matched: Britton, South Dakota, 1938, a boy at a town pool. Amateur film, no connection to the others but the leaving.
phase-matched and much too long: the 1933 fall, unbroken, in its own time.
larger consequence: a wall. Fire film, no one is letting go here, which is the point of the near-match.
the tank: a small splash, three men seated, a man with his back to us.
the longer hesitation that resists the pattern: someone stays up there.
ordinary release: hands put down a cloth and leave. Nothing follows. Sound is the bowling alley after the ball, from the third return, moved here on purpose.
